time_zone: NIST prints Eastern Daylight Time (UTC-4 on these dates). 'utc' is that time converted; 'nist_local_time' is the value as printed. The transcribers found two tables (questions 6 and 10) that run at UTC-5; their items say so in `note`.

part_notes.part_1.json: Section 6, questions 1-14 of the answer key (answers.txt lines 1013-1528, PDF pages 16-21; 'page' is the PDF page, as in eval/reference.json). One item per table row or stated fact. Q6 rows are split per timestamp. 'Considerations' cells are not transcribed, except that the NT hashes they list are quoted in the Q6 account rows (the table's NT Hash column points to them). Q1 prints no row for RM#1 and no answer to 'does the hash match'. TIME ZONES. Q1, Q2, Q4, Q5, Q7, Q9, Q13, Q14: no times printed. Q3: install date printed as GMT, copied. Q8: printed as 'Eastern Time + DST', UTC-4. Q11, Q12: caption '(Timezone is applied)', read as Eastern Daylight Time, UTC-4 (default rule; Q12's last shutdown 11:31:00 agrees with Q8's 11:31:05, and Q11's last run 11:28:47 falls before it). Q6, Q10: same caption, but the printed times run one hour behind the rest of the key, i.e. Eastern Standard Time, UTC-5, daylight saving not applied (Q4 prints the zone as UTC-05:00). utc for Q6 and Q10 is therefore printed time + 5 h, NOT the default + 4 h; every such item has a note giving the + 4 h value, so the choice can be reversed mechanically. Evidence, all from the key itself: (a) Q6 informant created 09:33:54 is 14:33:54 UTC at UTC-5, 32 s before the install date Q3 prints in GMT (14:34:26); at UTC-4 the account would be an hour older than the installation. (b) Q6 informant last login 2015-03-25 09:45:59; Q12 lists an event at 10:45:59 that day. (c) At UTC-4 the Q6 accounts would be created 10:51:54-10:53:01, before the day's first logon in Q12 (11:00:08). (d) Q10 Chrome installed 2015-03-22 10:11:51; Q15 has the Chrome installer download at 11:11:06 and Chrome's welcome page at 11:11:58. (e) Q10 Apple Software Update 2015-03-23 15:01:01; Q11 AppleSoftwareUpdateIco.exe 16:00:59. (f) Q10 .NET Framework 4 installed 2015-03-25 09:51:39; Q11 has its setup program first run at 10:50:15. (g) At UTC-4 Q10's Office install (10:04:14) would precede the OS install date. MATCHERS. systemSetting: fixed names only; rows with no fitting name are null. Q1 hash rows carry 'exhibit' from the table's Class column, PC included. Q2: aux_contains on the contract's 'start sector S, sectors C' wording. programInstalled: obj_contains the printed name, aux the printed version; manufacturer and path are in 'nist' only. programRun: obj is the file name (last part of the printed path), exact. aux: a path tail ('\folder\file', aux_contains) on Shimcache and MuiCache rows and on rows with no time; none on Prefetch and UserAssist rows that have a time, because those artifacts may record no path or spell the leading folders differently. Execution counts are in 'nist' only. Where the key lists one run from two sources (Prefetch and UserAssist at the same second) the two items have the same matchers. sessionEvent: Q12 prints no account, so no aux; Q6 last-login rows have aux = account name. accountSeen: no aux matcher, the key does not print the contract's wording.
part_notes.part_2.json: Part 2 of the NIST CFReDS Data Leakage Case answer key (dated 2018-07-23), section 6, questions listed in 'questions'. Only 'Possible Answer' rows are transcribed; values quoted under 'Considerations' are not items (they are mentioned in an item's note where they matter). 'page' is the PDF page (the '===== PAGE n =====' marker in answers.txt), not the number printed in the page footer, as in eval/reference.json. TIME ZONES. Q15, Q17, Q23, Q25, Q27, Q31: the table is marked '(Timezone is applied)', read as US Eastern local time; all dates are 2015-03-22 to 2015-03-25, inside daylight time, so utc = printed + 4 h. Q30: the 'Timestamp' column is marked '(Timezone is applied)' (utc = printed + 4 h); the 'Modified Time (UTC-05)' column is printed in UTC-05 (utc = printed + 5 h; January dates). Q18, Q19, Q20, Q24, Q29, Q32, Q34: the answer prints no time, so no utc and no local_day. CONVENTIONS. Q15: URLs split over several printed lines are joined with nothing in between; 72 URLs are matched exactly, 2 that the key prints cut off are matched with obj_contains. The Browser column is matched with aux_contains: 'Chrome' for Chrome, 'Internet Explorer' for the key's 'IE 8' and 'IE 11' (the key itself spells it out in question 13). Q23: the 48 printed rows are 24 renames; the timestamp cell spans a 'Renamed Old' and a 'Renamed New' row, and fileRenamed holds old name in obj and new name in aux, so there is one item per rename. Only file names are matched (obj_endswith old name, aux_contains new name) because the table header says 'just file names are OK'; the printed folders are in 'nist'. Q25, Q27: printed directory paths end in a backslash; the matcher drops it. ShellBag rows are folderOpened with aux_contains 'shell' (covers 'shell bag' and 'ShellBag'); '(created)' and '(last accessed)' differ only in the time. The drive letter (E:, V:) or \\server\share is kept in obj_endswith. The four JumpList / .LNK rows of Q27 are lnkTarget, as in questions 26, 28, 35. Two of those (Q27-13, Q27-14) have identical matchers because lnkTarget cannot tell a jump list from a .LNK file. Q29: files and folders named as traces are fileCreated (the file exists) or fileDeleted (marked '(deleted)'); the key's '\User\...' spelling is not corrected, only trailing path parts are matched. Q34: one item per listed file, fileCreated in the burn folder, no time printed. No 'exhibit' matcher is set anywhere: every row here is found on the PC image, including the Q25 rows about folders on RM#2. Inconsistencies copied as printed and flagged with 'note': Q19 (Office vs Outlook folder), Q29 (\User vs \Users, missing \Local), Q30 (the two modified times are swapped relative to the log excerpt).
part_notes.part_3.json: Part 3: section 6, questions 37-50, 52, 53, 54, 56, 57 of the NIST CFReDS Data Leakage answer key (2018-07-23). Worked from the answer key text and PDF and the row vocabulary only. 'page' is the PDF page (the '===== PAGE n =====' marker), as in eval/reference.json. TIME ZONES: Q37, Q44, Q45, Q46, Q47, Q48, Q52 carry the caption '(Timezone is applied)' = local time, US Eastern Daylight Time on these dates, utc = printed + 4 h. Q41 has no caption; read as local time (section 3 timeline). Q49 prints its own offsets: created times '(UTC-04)', modified times '(UTC-05)' (January), converted accordingly. Q52 Google Drive log lines print '-0400'; milliseconds dropped. Q38, Q39, Q40, Q42, Q43, Q50, Q53, Q54, Q56, Q57 print no times. GRANULARITY: one item per answer entity (a table row, an e-mail, a database record, a listed file), split per timestamp where a kind exists for that timestamp; attribute cells (size, format, checksum, body text, attachment) are quoted in 'nist' but are not separate items, as in Q21/Q55 of the existing reference. 'Considerations' blocks are not transcribed, except (a) values needed to fill a matcher of an answer row (Q47 shadow copy id) and (b) the Eraser rename chain that the Q52 wiping row points to with '(See below)' (Q52-34..41, marked in their notes). KIND CHOICES: file locations (Q38, Q40, Q42, Q47) are fileCreated with no time, as Q55 in the existing reference. Q44 rows are webVisit (URL exact, browser Internet Explorer); Q45 rows are emailSent with subject and time only, as Q21 in the existing reference (from/to are printed but not matched). Q46 rows are fileSeen / 'windows search index' with the printed Date Created; paths are printed with doubled backslashes, read as single separators. Q48 table rows are fileCreated and fileModified of the files inside the shadow copy; 'exists in VSC' sentences are fileSeen / 'shadow copy'. Q49: the deleted record is cloudFile 'google drive: deleted' (no time), its columns cloudFile created / modified. Q52: Search = webSearch, Download = fileDownloaded with the URL as source, Install/Run/Uninstall = programRun (executable name; printed path not matched), wiped files = fileDeleted on the day (a time range is printed), Shift+Delete and Google Drive 'Deleting file' = fileDeleted. Q52 rows 1, 2, 4 repeat Q16; Q45 repeats most of Q21. Q53 = fileCreated on RM#2 with aux containing 'unallocated space' (Q54: the old directory entries lie in unallocated areas). NOT TRANSCRIBED: Q58-Q60 lie in the line range given for Q57 but are not in this part's question list.
